_comment: Batch 020 -- the structural half of architecture Pri-B.
These are KIT PARTS, not rooms. The question a reviewer has to answer
is not 'is this a nice object' but 'does it belong to the same kit as
Batch 001', so the family sheet and the silhouette come first and the
in-situ frame -- the parts actually assembled into a bay -- comes last.
CAMERA FRAME (L-52): multi-model offsets are in the yawed frame, so x

K_bay_in_situ was first shot with a hand-placed `eye` and returned a photograph of the backdrop. `frame` solves its distance from the subject AABB and cannot miss the models; a guessed eye position can, and does so silently (L-62).

The family shot was first a four-model row 17 m wide. `frame` has to pick an axis to fit and picked the wrong one; staggering the row in z then hid the column behind a wall; and a hand-computed `look` missed the subject entirely. Two tight pairs is what the bench is good at, and comparing walls to walls is better evidence anyway (L-62).

K_grate is shot with backdrop 'none'. The grate is a RECESS anchored module_floor, and the bench stands an asset on a floor slab -- so the recess sank into the slab and the sheet showed its rim and nothing else. A part that is a hole cannot be photographed standing on a floor (L-63).
